sole_proprietorship.structure_note: A sole proprietorship is NOT a separately-formed legal entity in Texas -- there is no Certificate of Formation, no filing with the Secretary of State, and no board/shareholder/member governance structure, because the business and the owner are legally the same person. This file is deliberately leaner than every other entity-type file built so far (no identity/governance/meetings_notices/records_transparency categories in the corporate sense) because those categories genuinely don't apply, not because content was omitted by oversight. The single most important fact this file exists to carry: the owner has NO liability shield -- personal assets are fully exposed to business debts and claims, which is the defining legal difference between a sole proprietorship and every other entity type in this dataset. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30: (1) the only state-level filing that can apply is a county-level Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), and only if operating under a name other than the owner's own true legal name (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code Chapter 71) -- this is a county filing, not a Secretary of State filing, distinct from every other entity type in this dataset. (2) A true sole proprietorship is NOT subject to Texas franchise tax at all (Tex. Tax Code Section 171.0002(b)(1) and (d)), confirmed directly against the Texas Comptroller's own franchise tax overview publication -- this is a real structural difference from every other entity file, all of which include franchise tax/PIR filings. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: a single-member LLC that elects sole-proprietor tax treatment for federal purposes is NOT a sole proprietorship under Texas law and remains a taxable entity subject to franchise tax (Section 171.0002(d)) -- Texas looks at legal formation, not federal tax election. That case belongs in llc.json, not this file.

Assumed Name Certificate / DBA (County C: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code Chapter 71 -- filed with the county clerk in each county where the business maintains an office or conducts business (not the Secretary of State, which is the filing point only for registered entities like LLCs and corporations). Effective for a term not to exceed 10 years, renewable. A new certificate must generally be filed for changes in ownership, name, entity form, or location. Sections 71.202/71.203 provide criminal penalties for violations and fraudulent filing. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 via multiple cross-checked sources including county-clerk filing offices and the 2019 HB 3609 amendment history.
Sales Tax Permit / Sales Tax Filings (if: Tex. Tax Code Chapter 151 (Limited Sales, Excise, and Use Tax) -- applies to any seller of taxable goods or services regardless of entity type, including a sole proprietorship.
Workers' Compensation Policy (elective i: Tex. Labor Code Section 406.002 -- Texas is the only state in the country where workers' compensation coverage is elective, not mandatory, for most private employers. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 across multiple independent sources. An employer who opts out ('non-subscriber') must notify the Texas Division of Workers' Compensation (Section 406.004) and notify employees (Section 406.005), and forfeits certain common-law defenses in the event of a workplace injury lawsuit. EXCEPTION: coverage is mandatory for government building/construction contracts under Section 406.096. This same elective-not-mandatory status applies to every other entity-type file already built in this dataset (corporation, llc, nonprofit, pllc, pa, pc) -- none of those files currently carry this citation/caveat and are candidates for a follow-up correction.
Texas Business & Commerce Code Chapter 7: Same Chapter 71 basis as the Assumed Name Certificate entry above -- listed again under statutory for visibility in that category's context.
